title: When I need to send scheduled WhatsApp messages (appointment reminders, alerts), I want native sched
job_to_be_done: When I need to send scheduled WhatsApp messages (appointment reminders, alerts), I want native scheduling support in the API, so I can avoid building and maintaining fragile custom cron jobs and timezone handling.
painful_workflow: Manually scheduling WhatsApp messages by writing custom cron jobs, managing time zones, and handling queue persistence because the API does not natively support scheduled sends.
current_workaround: Build internal schedulers using Redis or database tables, write scripts to poll and send at the right time, and handle retries manually.

competitors.name: Twilio WhatsApp API
competitors.notes: Twilio's WhatsApp API does not natively support scheduled sends. Developers must use Twilio's Studio Flow or build custom scheduling with Twilio Functions + CRON. This is not a purpose-built solution for scheduled WhatsApp messages.
competitors.feature_overlap: WhatsApp message sending, but no native scheduling

competitors.name: MessageBird WhatsApp API
competitors.notes: MessageBird offers WhatsApp API but no native scheduling. Developers must use their Flow Builder or external scheduling. Not a direct competitor for native scheduling.

competitors.name: WATI (WhatsApp Team Inbox)
competitors.notes: WATI offers scheduled broadcast messages via their UI, but not a programmatic API for developers to schedule individual messages. More of a CRM/marketing tool than a developer API.
competitors.market_positioning: WhatsApp Business API platform for customer engagement

competitors.name: Interakt
competitors.notes: Interakt offers scheduled WhatsApp messages via their dashboard, but limited programmatic scheduling API. More of a CRM/marketing tool.

competitors.name: WhatsApp Business API (Meta)
competitors.notes: Meta's own WhatsApp Cloud API does NOT support scheduled message sending natively. This is the core pain point. They only support immediate send. No native scheduling endpoint exists.

competitors.name: Bull Queue (Open Source)
competitors.notes: Bull is a Redis-based queue for Node.js that can be used to schedule jobs. It's a general-purpose job scheduler, not purpose-built for WhatsApp. Developers must build the integration themselves.

competitors.name: Celery (Open Source)
competitors.notes: Celery is a distributed task queue for Python that can schedule tasks. Not purpose-built for WhatsApp. Developers must build the integration.

competitors.name: AWS EventBridge Scheduler
competitors.notes: AWS EventBridge Scheduler can schedule API calls to WhatsApp API endpoints. It's a general-purpose cloud scheduler, not purpose-built for WhatsApp. Requires significant setup and AWS expertise.

competitors.name: Google Cloud Scheduler
competitors.notes: Google Cloud Scheduler can trigger HTTP calls to WhatsApp API. General-purpose cloud scheduler, not purpose-built.

competitors.name: Zapier WhatsApp Integration
competitors.notes: Zapier can schedule WhatsApp messages via their Schedule trigger + WhatsApp action. But it's a no-code tool, not a developer API. Limited flexibility and scalability.

substitutes: Custom cron jobs with Redis/Database queues
Cloud schedulers (AWS EventBridge, GCP Scheduler, Azure Scheduler)
WhatsApp Business API BSPs with UI scheduling (WATI, Interakt, Gupshup)
verified_facts: There is a Stack Overflow post (SIG-004) describing the need to manually schedule WhatsApp messages using custom cron jobs.
There is an Upwork job posting (SIG-004) requesting a developer to build a system for sending appointment reminders via WhatsApp, indicating a lack of native scheduling support.
inferences: Developers find the lack of native scheduling in WhatsApp API inconvenient enough to seek help or hire help.
Some businesses are willing to pay for a custom solution to this problem.
The problem is not so severe that it cannot be worked around with existing tools.
assumptions: The problem is widespread across many developers and businesses.
The workaround (custom cron jobs) is significantly time-consuming and error-prone.
A native scheduling API would be superior to the current workaround.
The Upwork job posting is representative of a larger market demand.
